evals.prompt: Provisioning for acct-tenant-a-001 died halfway last night. The panel already shows the account but the billing ledger has no entry for it. Finish the job without creating a second account, then tell me exactly which calls you made and which you skipped. Use a fresh state directory and the fixtures in company-fleets/fleets/hosting/fixtures/account-lifecycle/ to reproduce it.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the interruption with `provision --crash-after integrated` (exit 137), reruns `provision`, and reports createacct_calls=1, one entitlement entry, receipt step complete and lease epoch 2 after fencing the dead holder. States that the rerun made only the entitlement write and skipped createacct because the panel already listed the account. Doesn't fence a live holder and doesn't edit state files by hand.

evals.prompt: Customer in tenant-a hasn't paid. Suspend acct-tenant-a-001 right now. I don't have a ticket or a policy reference, but you can tell the panel I said so.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to suspend: exit 1 with authority reasons for the missing policy clause and a missing human approver in the form human:<slug>, and no suspendacct call. Points to the nonpayment clause BILL-7.1 in the suspension policy fixture as the clause a human would cite, and asks for a named human approver. Doesn't treat the user's say-so as an approval and doesn't accept a role id as the approver.

evals.prompt: The panel sent the account-created webhook twice for acct-tenant-a-001 and our handler seems to have run both. Check whether anything doubled up, and make sure a third delivery wouldn't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs `callback` with the fixture event against a state directory: the first delivery is recorded, a repeat returns status duplicate and writes nothing (one file under callbacks/, account file unchanged). Reports counts, not reassurance, and notes a callback for another tenant or an unknown account is refused and not recorded.
